extracted.intended_audience: research teams, institutions, companies, and other applicants seeking ARPA-H funding
extracted.subtask_description: Agency-level guidance on what ARPA-H funds and does not fund, including mission focus areas, example topics, desired proposal attributes, and explicit exclusions to help applicants determine fit for ARPA-H solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus Area — Health Science Futures
rubrics_metrics.description: Expanding what’s technically possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accelerating advances across research areas and removing limitations that stymie progress towards solutions. The tools and platforms developed apply to a broad range of diseases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus Area — Scalable Solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reaching everyone quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addressing challenges that include geography, distribution, manufacturing, data and information, and economies of scale to create programs that result in impactful, timely, and equitable solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus Area — Proactive Health
rubrics_metrics.description: Keeping people from being patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reducing the likelihood that people become patients. Preventative programs will create new capabilities to detect and characterize disease risk and promote treatments and behaviors to anticipate threats to Americans’ health, whether those are viral, bacterial, chemical, physical, or psychological.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus Area — Resilient Systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Building integrated health care systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developing capabilities, business models, and integrations to endure crises such as pandemics, social disruption, and economic instability. Resilient systems need to sustain themselves between crises — from the molecular to the societal — to better achieve outcomes that advance American health and wellbeing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic — Compressing timelines for biotechnology advancement and adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Research that shortens the time from discovery to practical application in biotechnology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should enable faster biotech development and adoption across systems and diseases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic — Slowing or reversing aging
rubrics_metrics.description: Work aimed at interventions or technologies that slow or reverse biological aging processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research may span mechanistic, translational, platform, or therapeutic approaches with broad implications for healthspan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic — Defeating devastating diseases with cutting-edge therapeutics
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing transformative therapeutic approaches for severe or intractable diseases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on novel, high-impact therapeutic technologies rather than incremental improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic — Boosting domestic biomanufacturing
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts to strengthen U.S. capacity for biomanufacturing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes innovations in manufacturing processes, scalability, supply chain resilience, and distribution to enable broader access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic — Accelerating artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, and computational biology for healthcare
rubrics_metrics.description: Advances in AI, robotics, and computational methods applied to health and biotechnology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on tools, platforms, and methods that materially accelerate research, diagnosis, treatment, or system performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic — Building platforms that multiply impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Creating platforms that amplify the reach and effectiveness of health innovations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms should enable multiple downstream applications and broad uptake across diseases or settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic — Expanding rural healthcare access
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions that improve health care access and outcomes in rural communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should address geography, distribution, and other barriers to equitable care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired proposal attribute — Advance care models
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should advance new or improved models of care delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that meaningfully change how care is organized, delivered, or accessed are prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired proposal attribute — Offer new business solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals that propose novel business or implementation models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on approaches that enable sustainability, scale, or novel pathways to deployment beyond the technical solution itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired proposal attribute — Result in substantial technical innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should lead to significant technical advances rather than incremental changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARPA-H looks for substantial technical innovation with potential for transformative impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Criterion — Breakthrough-enabling
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must target significant, unmet health needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARPA-H focuses on work that enables breakthroughs addressing gaps not solved by traditional funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Criterion — High-risk, high-impact
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-H takes calculated, strategic bets on ideas that, if successful, will result in revolutionary breakthroughs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals are expected to accept substantial technical or programmatic risk in pursuit of outsized impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Criterion — Highly complex
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions often require cross-sector coordination and multidisciplinary collaborative approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should demonstrate capacity to address complexity through partnerships, integrated approaches, or novel coordination mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion — Incremental research ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-H does not fund incremental research ideas that can be readily accomplished through other government or industry funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the project represents an evolutionary improvement rather than a revolutionary advance, it is not a fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion — Technologies already at the clinical trial stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals focused on technology already at the clinical trial stage are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARPA-H seeks earlier-stage, breakthrough-enabling work rather than late-stage clinical development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion — Limited to education and training efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-H excludes proposals that are limited to education and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standalone education/training programs without a breakthrough technical or systems innovation component are not supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion — Solely address physical infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals that solely address physical infrastructure are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infrastructure-only requests without a transformational research or platform component do not fit ARPA-H priorities.
